extracted.intended_audience: scholars, historians of mathematics, and editors/translators of classical mathematical texts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing a critical/modern edition of Archimedes: selecting manuscripts, presenting text in modern notation, writing introductions and notes, and documenting editorial decisions and evidence. Aimed at producing a faithful but readable scholarly edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithful reproduction of the treatises
rubrics_metrics.description: My main object has been to present a perfectly faithful reproduction of the treatises as they have come down to us, neither adding anything nor leaving out anything essential or important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain the content of the received text; avoid adding material or omitting anything essential. Use notes to illuminate points rather than altering the main text. Emphasize fidelity to the transmitted works while aiding modern readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain original numbering and enunciate propositions near the original
rubrics_metrics.description: It has been possible to retain the numbering of the propositions and to enunciate them in a manner more nearly approaching the original without thereby making the enunciations obscure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the original proposition numbering for cross-reference and historical integrity; adapt enunciations toward the original wording as far as readability allows, avoiding obscurity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use modern notation with reasonable uniformity
rubrics_metrics.description: Edited in modern notation ... the subject matter is not so complicated as to necessitate absolute uniformity in the notation used (which is the only means whereby Apollonius can be made even tolerably readable), though I have tried to secure as much uniformity as was fairly possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt modern mathematical notation to improve accessibility, but balance uniformity with faithfulness; full, rigid standardization is not always required or desirable if it harms clarity or fidelity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use bracketed, in-line notes to clarify propositions when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: The notes are for the most part intended to throw light on particular points in the text or to supply proofs of propositions assumed by Archimedes as known; sometimes I have thought it right to insert within square brackets after certain propositions, and in the same type, notes designed to bring out the exact significance of those propositions, in cases where to place such notes in the Introduction or at the bottom of the page might lead to their being overlooked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When explanatory material would be missed in an Introduction or footnote, place brief clarifying notes immediately after the relevant enunciation in square brackets and in the same typeface to ensure they are noticed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefatory historical and methodological discussion; mark speculative hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Much of the Introduction is, as will be seen, historical; the rest is devoted partly to giving a more general view of certain methods employed by Archimedes and of their mathematical significance ... where it is necessary to put forward hypotheses for the purpose of explaining obscure points, I have been careful to call attention to their speculative character, though I have given the historical evidence where such can be quoted in support of a particular hypothesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate historical exposition from methodological discussion; when conjectural explanations are advanced, explicitly label them speculative and provide whatever historical evidence exists so readers can evaluate plausibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a comprehensive list of principal works consulted
rubrics_metrics.description: LIST OF THE PRINCIPAL WORKS CONSULTED.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document all major editions, commentaries, translations, and relevant secondary literature consulted in preparing the edition to support textual and historical claims and to guide future scholarship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript provenance and selection based on paleography and relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: The MSS. of the best class all had a common origin in a MS. which ... is described ... and all the evidence goes to show that it was written as early as the 9th or 10th century. ... The three most important MSS. extant are: F, B, C. Of these it is certain that B was copied from the Valla MS. ... From notes and paleographic features one infers relations among witnesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace manuscript genealogy, date and localize witnesses, record notes in copies (e.g., 'most ancient'), and use paleography and internal notes (abbreviations, lacunae) to infer archetypes and the relative authority of extant codices before choosing readings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer the most trustworthy manuscript(s) when evidence supports it
rubrics_metrics.description: The natural inference from all the evidence is that F, B and C all had their origin in the Valla MS.; and of the three F is the most trustworthy. For (1) the extreme care with which the copyist of F kept to the original ... and (2) there is no doubt that the writer of B was somewhat of an expert and made many alterations on his own authority, not always with success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When manuscripts diverge, prefer the witness shown (by provenance, fidelity to archetype, and characteristic errors) to most closely reflect the original; document the reasons for favoring one witness over another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document lacunae, worn/illegible folios, and scribal notes
rubrics_metrics.description: A short preface to C states that the first page of the archetype was so rubbed and worn with age that not even the name of Archimedes could be read upon it ... in F the first page was apparently left blank at first and afterwards written in by a different hand with many gaps, while in B there are similar deficiencies and a note attached by the copyist is to the effect that the first page of the archetype was indistinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly record places where the archetype or copies are illegible or missing, reproduce copyist marginalia about defects, and indicate reconstructions or conjectures made to fill lacunae.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collate translations and earlier editions to resolve readings
rubrics_metrics.description: Pope Nicholas V. had a MS. of Archimedes which he caused to be translated into Latin ... From the fact that the translation of Jacobus Cremonensis has the same lacuna as that in F, B and C ... it seems clear that the translator had before him either the Valla MS. itself or (more likely) a copy of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use medieval and early modern translations and printed editions (Latin, German, prior editors) as independent witnesses to readings and lacunae; compare their orders and variants to infer the archetype and transcription history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful reproduction of figures and vigilance about letter/figure confusion
rubrics_metrics.description: It appears to have been carefully copied from an original ... and it contained figures drawn for the most part with great care and accuracy, but there was considerable confusion between the letters in the figures and those in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reproducing or typesetting diagrams, check alignment of letter-labels in figures vs. running text; note places where earlier copyists have confused figure letters and correct only with clear justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial restraint in including images or portraits lacking authority
rubrics_metrics.description: I was particularly anxious to place ... a portrait of Archimedes ... I was now informed ... that there does not appear to be any authority for any one of the three [portraits] ... I was, therefore, reluctantly obliged to give up my idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include purported portraits or iconographic material unless there is reliable evidence or authority; prefer omission to presenting unsupported images as authentic.
